title: Make MainWindow's outcome panel scroll or tab, and decide its minimum window size, before the next analysis panel is added
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: The outcome panel is restructured to scroll or tab (rather than a hand-tuned fixed Grid of star rows with per-section MinHeights) so that sections keep fitting as new ones are added: missing
The panel is ready for the next analysis panels (largest folders, by-extension) to be added to this same Grid without breaking the fit: missing

Does the person ever want two analysis sections visible at once (for example largest files beside by-extension)? Tabs preclude it, and the slice title allowed 'scroll or tab'. If yes, the next slices need a splitter or a second tab host, and that changes the 'one section = one TabItem' contract.

Tabs vs. a splitter or stacked sections. Tabs show one section at a time, so 'Largest files' and the unreadable list can no longer be seen together, which SL-046's note about a splitter wanted. The unreadable list was already on demand behind an Expander.
Unreadable tab hidden at N=0 vs. shown but disabled. Hidden matches the Expander today and C-001, and disabled would keep the strip width constant.
Count in the tab header vs. in the tab content. Only the unreadable tab carries a count here, and any other text goes in the content.
Flat named report keys per TabItem, in the existing style, vs. one generic OutcomeTabs.tabs array that needs no reporter edit per section.
MaxHeight cap on the texts vs. a proportional row for it. The cap is simpler and keeps today's numbers.

Design cases C-012 (a third TabItem), C-013 (keyboard switching) and C-014 (125%/150% scaling) are marked material:false in the design and have no fixture; the rule is written in the XAML comment instead.

No test with four headers (Largest files, Largest folders, By extension, Unreadable folders (N)) at 560: only two tabs exist, O-003 settled that they fit, and the slices that add those sections own the fixture. stripRows is asserted with the two real tabs, including the 5-digit count.

No xUnit twin for the new ScrollViewer rule: it sits below '# settled by SL-065' in .taad/fitness.yaml (the engine added it), and by that file's convention settled entries have no ArchitectureRulesTests Fact. rules-parity counts it as settled and reports AGREE.

The plant rows S09/S10 were not measured through eng/rules-harness/harness.py: the harness exits 2 (CANNOT MEASURE) at this HEAD, before any row runs, for an unrelated reason (see follow-ups). They were measured directly with the engine's taad3.fitness.check on scratch copies planted exactly as the harness would plant them: S09 fired at line 107 and S10 at line 110, both at offset 0 as recorded, with no hit on the clean tree.

WindowCases.ps1 Update-App republishes only when the exe is older than the newest source. A non-bundle apphost (359 KB, framework-dependent) left in artifacts/publish made every window case time out, and SL-065's build check put that down to 'no interactive window station'. Update-App (and read-window) should refuse an exe that is not the single-file bundle, for example by size or by checking for the bundle marker.

eng/rules-harness/harness.py cannot measure at this HEAD: taad3.fitness reports the must_not_import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks' as UNRAN when the scratch copy has no code graph, and check_clean refuses. Options: call fitness.check(tree, build=True), or teach check_clean about known-unran import rules. Then run S09/S10 through it.

The person-run network pass (N-001..N-004 plus StalledShareTests, docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md) is stale by its own path rule: MainWindow.xaml(.cs), tests/window/FsaWindowHook/** and WindowCases.ps1 all changed here.

The texts cap is a fixed 76 px at every size. A whole-drive ending (volume line wrapping, then elapsed; about 107 px) or one with notes scrolls even when maximized. If the person dislikes that, the rejected taste alternative was a proportional texts row.

Still open for the person (design-slice): should two sections ever be visible at once (a splitter, or a second tab host)? That would change the 'one section = one TabItem' contract before the largest-folders and by-extension slices.

Validate's own obligations O-001 (unselected section adds nothing and reads inView=false) and O-002 (strip stays one row) now have runnable evidence in S-002/B-007 (OutcomeTabs height kept across the click, lists' inView flipped) and S-007 (stripRows=1 with 'Unreadable folders (12,345)').
The largest-folders and by-extension slices should add a four-header stripRows check at MinWidth 560 with the real headers, and their own report keys per the contract in the XAML comment.
